slides.title: One dataset, two governed consumption paths
slides.takeaway: Advisor computes recommendations once, then serves customer and internal teams through independently governed publication paths.
slides.subtitle: Azure Resource Graph serves customers; internal Kusto serves first-party teams. Each path enforces its own authorization scope.

diagram.alt: Three-layer architecture showing Advisor computing recommendations once, publishing them to Azure Resource Graph and internal Kusto, then applying customer Azure RBAC and internal TPID authorization.

sources.label: Query for Advisor data in Azure Resource Graph

slides.notes:
Purpose: explain, for an internal engineering and support audience, how a single Advisor recommendation dataset is published to two different consumption surfaces with two different authorization models.

Flow (left to right):
1. Data production and distribution — the Advisor engine computes recommendations on a schedule into recommendation datasets (snapshots, scores, tracking metadata). Those datasets are synced to Azure Resource Graph (ARG) and exported/ingested into internal first-party (1P) Kusto clusters.
2. Customer experience — customers query Advisor through ARM / ARG endpoints; Azure RBAC authorizes access scoped to subscription, resource group, and tenant, so each customer sees only their own recommendation data.
3. Internal 1P analytics — the 1P Kusto clusters hold Advisor data for all customers. A TPID authorization layer applies TPID-based RBAC that partitions data by TPID (tenants and subscriptions). CSAM and support/account personas can read only the TPIDs assigned to them; an admin persona bypasses TPID scoping for full access.

Authorization models summarized:
- Customer path: Azure RBAC via ARM/ARG. Scope = subscription → resource group → tenant.
- Internal path: TPID-based RBAC in Kusto. Scope = TPID → tenants → subscriptions.
- Admin path: admin role in Kusto. Scope = all TPIDs (all customer data).

Key points: the same Advisor data is delivered to multiple experiences; external and internal usage use different authorization models; internal Kusto contains data for all customers; TPID is the top-level security boundary for internal usage. Access to Kusto is audited and remains within Microsoft internal boundaries. ARG and Kusto exports run on a scheduled cadence to keep data fresh.

Sourcing note: Azure Advisor and its availability in Azure Resource Graph are public (see sources). The internal 1P Kusto clusters, TPID authorization model, and CSAM/support/admin personas are drawn from the provided internal description and are not documented in public Microsoft sources; treat them as conceptual internal architecture, not a verified deployed topology. Confirm cadence, audit, and exact scope wording with the owning team before external use.
